title: Violin with Maclo Williams, Talladega, and the Tuskegee dance orchestra
summary: He switched to violin after hearing orchestra director Williams, played viola at Talladega, but piano reading let him join the dance orchestra and start a professional path.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, when did you decide you thought you could kind of make it pretty good on the piano?

Oh, I don't know -- I lost interest a little bit in the piano when I heard the orchestra director, Maclo Williams, play the violin, as a young kid, you know -- I must have been about 10 or 11 then, and I suppose nothing would satisfy me but -- I asked my mother to get me a violin; I wanted to play the violin like Mr. Williams did, you see.
And so he taught me -- but I played the violin all through high school, and still in college, I took up the viola because they needed a viola player.

Taladega College, yes. But after school, there wasn't enough drive, really, to stay with the violin, the oboe and the clarinet because of the actual practical reality of being able to work at the piano, see, and I had gotten into, after studying with Mrs. Simms and learning to read the piano, you know, you have to read the bass clef, treble clef, I was able to play in the dance orchestra
where you didn't have to be a virtuoso, but you could read a stock orchestration which is written -- that's all that was sufficient, to play for the dances.

And so that started, really, a career right there in Tuskegee, playing in the dance orchestra. But the classical foundation, and having learned to read, stood me in good stature. We had these stock orchestrations. Right. And then that branched on out to more advanced ear playing and improvising by ear, and then a professional career in jazz.
